content.title: About
content.content: Apple pie filling is a ready‑made mixture of fresh apples, sugar, spices and sometimes lemon juice, designed for quick and convenient preparation of apple pie. Apples are sliced, combined with cinnamon, nutmeg and sweetened, then the filling is ready to use.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional American filling often mixes sweet and tart apple varieties for balanced flavor.
Cinnamon added to the filling provides antioxidant benefits and enhances aroma.
Classic recipes sometimes include a bit of butter to make the filling juicier.
Apple filling can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 3 months.
There are sugar‑free versions that rely on the natural sweetness of apples and a touch of honey.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Apples contain soluble and insoluble fiber that supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in apples helps boost the immune system and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in apples protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Fiber and potassium help lower cholesterol levels and maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Apple pie filling contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Prepared fillings often contain added sugar, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes or those limiting sugar intake.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to cinnamon or nutmeg, causing allergic reactions.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The natural acidity of apples can irritate a sensitive stomach in some people.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions may contain preservatives that are not preferred by all consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the filling as the base for apple pie, stir into muffins, pastries, pancakes, or serve warm as a dessert with ice cream. It can also be mixed with cottage cheese or yogurt for a healthy snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags – up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge or at room temperature before use.
